How it was scored

  • Scanned with OpenSCAP in the image build on 2026-10-17 16:13 UTC.
  • Content: SCAP Security Guide 0.1.82, profile “DISA STIG for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9” (xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_stig), with the refined value listed below.
  • Score = rules passed ÷ (rules passed + rules failed). Every rule listed under Exemptions failed in the scan and counts as a failure in the score. Not-applicable and not-checked rules are not scored.
  • The build's OpenSCAP gate was enforced: floor 90%, and no failing rule without a documented exemption.
  • FIPS mode is enabled, using the OS vendor's FIPS cryptographic modules.
  • Red Hat Enterprise Linux images are BYOL: you supply your own Red Hat subscription. StigReady does not sell or provide Red Hat commercial licenses.

An OpenSCAP score measures this image against SSG content. It is not a certification, authorization or accreditation, and it is not an assessment of your system.

Exemptions (16)

Each rule below fails in the image for the reason given, and the last column is what you do to meet it on your instance. The reasons and actions come from the build record (the signed POA&M lists the same rules).

RuleSTIG IDCategoryWhy it fails in the imageWhat you do
grub2_admin_username
Set the Boot Loader Admin Username to a Non-Default Value		RHEL-09-212020AWS Marketplace policy: you complete it after launchAWS Marketplace policy prohibits meeting this rule in an AMI: "AMI must not contain hardcoded secrets such as system user and service passwords (including hashed passwords)" and "Password-based authentication for instance services is prohibited. This applies even if the password is generated, reset, or defined by the user at launch"; Linux AMIs "must allow users to get fully privileged access (for example, to allow sudo access)" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/product-and-ami-policies.html). The rule needs a boot loader or root password hash in the image, or a sudo password for the key-only default user.After launch run sudo stigready-set-credentials (installed in the image): it sets your own GRUB superuser and password, root password and a sudo password for your admin user, and removes NOPASSWD, which meets this rule on your instance.

Configure Fapolicy Module to Employ a Deny-all, Permit-by-exception Policy to Allow the Execution of Authorized Software Programs.		RHEL-09-433016Cloud usability: you configure it after launchA default-deny fapolicyd allowlist blocks dnf, Ansible and every customer workload not in the list on a general-purpose image.Build an allowlist for your workloads, then set fapolicyd to deny-by-default.
network_configure_name_resolution
Configure Multiple DNS Servers in /etc/resolv.conf		RHEL-09-252035Cloud usability: you configure it after launchThe rule wants two DNS servers in resolv.conf. On EC2 the VPC resolver is supplied by DHCP; the AMI owner manages DNS.Configure at least two name servers for your network, or keep the VPC resolver per your policy.
selinux_context_elevation_for_sudo
Elevate The SELinux Context When An Administrator Calls The Sudo Command		RHEL-09-431016Cloud usability: you configure it after launchThe STIG's sudoers line (TYPE=sysadm_t ROLE=sysadm_r) makes sudo fail for the default unconfined_u login, so the image would have no working administrator.Map your admin users to staff_u/sysadm_u, then add the TYPE/ROLE sudoers line.
sysctl_user_max_user_namespaces_no_remediation
Disable the use of user namespaces		RHEL-09-213105Cloud usability: you configure it after launchThe STIG itself says to set a non-zero value where containers run; rootless containers and sandboxes need user namespaces.Set user.max_user_namespaces=0 if the instance runs no containers or sandboxes.

configure_opensc_card_drivers
Configure opensc Smart Card Drivers		RHEL-09-611160Smart card / CAC: needs your PKISmart card (CAC/PIV) login needs a card reader and the customer's own PKI: their CA certificates, OCSP/CRL endpoints and certificate-to-user mapping. A cloud instance has no reader, and no CA or mapping we could ship is correct for any customer. Some of these rules only install or enable a package; they are exempt with the class so the image does not run a smart card stack that cannot be used, and the customer enables it with their PKI.If you use CAC/PIV: install opensc and pcsc-lite, enable pcscd, install your CA bundle, and configure SSSD (or pam_pkcs11 on Ubuntu) certificate verification, OCSP/CRL and the certificate mapping for your directory.

Refined values

var_accounts_authorized_local_users_regex: The SSG default list of local accounts, plus the accounts this image itself has: ec2-user, unbound, fapolicyd, postfix.

Value used: ^(root|bin|daemon|adm|lp|sync|shutdown|halt|mail|operator|games|ftp|nobody|tss|systemd-coredump|dbus|polkitd|avahi|colord|rtkit|pipewire|clevis|sssd|geoclue|flatpak|setroubleshoot|libstoragemgmt|systemd-oom|gdm|cockpit-ws|cockpit-wsinstance|gnome-initial-setup|sshd|chrony|dnsmasq|tcpdump|admin|ec2-user|unbound|fapolicyd|postfix)$
